title: A Low-Space Algorithm for Worst-Case Subset Sum
main_claim: A uniform randomized one-sided-error algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum that runs in poly(n)·2^{n/2} time and uses O(u^15·2^{0.199n}) writable words on every run, for each fixed polynomial bound b ≤ n^c on the bit length (Theorem 1.1; Corollary: O(2^{n/5}) space).
coverage: I read all of the LaTeX: the introduction, the preliminaries (deficiency martingale variance, entropy constants, prime lemma), the streams and bounded dictionaries, the compression trial, the representation layout and filters, prefix accounting, survival, resources, separators and implementation. I re-derived these by hand: the compression exponents (3a+r_L ≤ .4475n+4δ+ε, 4a+r_R ≤ .5n, bucket expectation 2^{.1985n} < C); the leaf-size identity β_j/2 = r/8 + H̄_0·m/4 + H̄_j·m/2 and the bound β_j/2 ≤ .181052n; the feasibility of r_j and r_ji; Γ, Λ and ξ; all three exponent relations; the tuple exponent bound ≤ n/2 (excess −.0662m+.0156n < 0); the third relation's margin ≈ .0017n ≥ .0015n; and the M_0-largest/spread-test bounds on f_0 and f_max. I checked the survival chain (balance, concentration, orientation, guesses, multinomial subblock survival, Cauchy–Schwarz residue coverage, nested p_j | p_0) and the u^-100 product. I checked the left and right bucket arguments (equal-weight entries ≤ binom(m,k_0) ≤ 2^{.1947n} < C/2; the prefix path ends in a completed task) and the three prefix-accounting bounds. For the separator I checked coverage, the incidence charging and the right-side complement reduction. I verified numerically that E(k) ≤ 1−h(1/4) on [1/6,1/3]; the maximum is exactly 0 at k=1/4, which matches the paper's concavity argument. I also checked the word-width and space bookkeeping and the amplification step (u^120 rounds against u^-110 success per round). The compression lemma's high-mean case and the representation trial's low-mean case cover all inputs. I did not check the citation-level details of BCKM24 or NW21; the paper re-proves the parts it uses.
sibling_notes: The family-138 board was empty when I started. The paper is self-contained and re-proves the residue-coverage, separator and stream lemmas it uses from NW21, BCKM24 and SS81. Some exponents have zero exponential slack (ξ+Γ ≤ n/2 has margin ≈ −0.0011m; the separator entropy is tight at k=1/4); in both places only polynomial factors are absorbed, and that is handled correctly.
